**Indikator 16** is a supplementary clinical quality indicator utilized within the Danish healthcare system to monitor the long-term outcomes of patients newly diagnosed with atrial fibrillation [^src1]. Specifically, the metric tracks the proportion of these newly diagnosed patients who develop [[hjertesvigtsindikatoren]] (heart failure) within one year of their initial diagnosis [^src1]. It serves as a critical tool for evaluating the incidence of heart failure as a direct complication of atrial fibrillation, complementing other core metrics such as Indikator 10, which tracks mortality among prevalent atrial fibrillation patients [^src1].

The indicator is a central component of the annual reporting from the Danish Atrial Fibrillation Database (Databasen for Atrieflimren i Danmark), which is published by the Regions' Clinical Quality Development Programme (RKKP) [^src1]. To ensure statistical precision and methodological transparency, the data underpinning Indikator 16 is derived from rigorous registry linkages between the Danish National Patient Registry (Landspatientregisteret) and the Civil Registration System (CPR-registeret) [^src1]. The reported findings include comparable figures from previous years alongside confidence intervals, and the data is broken down at national, regional, and municipal levels to support localized clinical quality development [^src1]. 

Chronologically, the specific reporting period for Indikator 16 detailed in the 2023 annual report covers the timeframe from July 1, 2021, to June 30, 2022 [^src1]. The comprehensive statistical analyses and detailed breakdowns for this indicator are formally presented on page 110 of the report [^src1]. Through this granular tracking, Indikator 16 reinforces RKKP's role as the national governing body for clinical quality improvement in Denmark [^src1].
